Death Bringing Cobra (S30) / Umbral Covenant (S90) Campaign Chain

Region (English ranking partition): Sarhal.

Starting country: Death Bringing Cobra (S30) Formable: Umbral Covenant (S90)

In brief: This exceptionally long, evil campaign begins with a mountain warlord’s bargain with witches and ends with an empire of interplanar suffering consuming Sarhal. The first ten missions are a formation prologue; Umbral Covenant’s 87 missions combine expansion, shadow rifts, mage projects, and a sacrificial endgame into a distinctive but demanding conquest loop.

Story: Very high | Mission-tree length: Extra-long (10 direct S30 missions and 87 direct S90 missions) | Mission-tree update: verified locally for v1.37.5.0 | Uniqueness: Very high | Tedium: High | Early pressure: High | Expansion: Very high

Identity and history

Death Bringing Cobra (S30) is the 1444 starting country; Umbral Covenant (S90) is the successor formed directly at the end of its mission prologue. The current local localisation renders their names as “Death Bringing Cobra” and “Umbral Covenant.” Other eligible Shadow Pact countries in Sarhal can also form S90 by a general decision; S30 is the dedicated campaign entry, with its own ten-mission prologue, formation event, and successor narrative branches. [Local script; local localisation]

S30’s ruler, Kuende “the Giftbringer,” comes from an old order destroyed by a purge war. A 1439 coup and war forced her into the mountains. The Chinese source summarises her hag bargain as sacrificing kin and an unborn child for power, troops and revenge. The current English opening scene needs a narrower reading: Kuende says her kin and partner are already dead at her enemies’ hands, and offers her unborn child to Ilfanill. This is not evidence that she personally killed those relatives, or that the child died; the later Vile One is that child. By 1444 she is a warlord of the Shadow Pact faith with several schools of magic, ruling through war, sacrifice, and omens. [Local history script; local narrative text]

The offline Wiki’s Coven of Yezel Mora entry identifies the Death Bringing Cobra clan leader as someone personally cultivated by Ilfanill, and says she exchanged her child for hag-borne power; that child later became “The Vile One.” This is consistent with the local prologue. A separate “Shadow Covenant” Wiki entry, however, describes a worldwide secret organization originating among assassins of Jaher. The similar names do not establish that it is the same entity as the formable Umbral Covenant. [Wiki background; evidence boundary]

National story and campaign arc

The Death Bringing Cobra prologue is not a long nation-building phase but an accelerated descent. Use shadow warriors, omens, and a war economy to subdue neighboring warlords, claim the witches’ three “gifts,” and transform directly into S90 through the final event, switching ideas and mission trees. This is more than a simple rename: the Vile One becomes a powerful immortal mage-ruler, and the country is remade as a theocratic magocracy. [Local script; official dev diary]

Umbral Covenant’s main arc has four parts: maintain a dangerous alliance with the Coven of Yezel Mora; gather suffering, knowledge, and magic across Sarhal; conquer territory to create shadow rifts and expand shadow-essence capacity; and complete three major magical projects, pushing the mortal realm toward planar convergence. Dynamic regional missions make the direction of conquest respond to the campaign, so 87 direct missions do not mean that all 87 fixed slots appear in every run. [Local script]

The final ritual reveals that the ruler and the Coven are not equals. The script prepares two endings: obey the ritual, at the explicit cost of “losing the game,” or betray the witches and try to survive. The ordinary mission trigger for the non-betrayal ending is statically disabled; whether another runtime event completes that ending still requires in-game verification. [Local script; unresolved]

Core mechanics

Shadow warriors and omens. S30 uses a special army and Shadow Pact religious rituals to establish military advantage quickly. Shadow warriors are powerful but costly in manpower and corruption; omens and rituals can accelerate formation while also creating continuing governance costs. The ten missions are designed to end the warlord period quickly, not to sustain a long S30 campaign. [Local script; official dev diary]

Shadow Empowerments and Shadow Essence. After formation, open the dedicated page in the government interface and choose abilities from five categories: Spirit, Shadow, Twilight, and the later-unlocked Soul and Abyss categories. Each empowerment occupies Shadow Essence capacity, with stronger tiers requiring higher upkeep; switching incurs a cooldown of about five years. Conquering more territory and establishing major and minor rifts increases capacity, making “conquer a region → create a rift → configure another empowerment” the central loop. [Local script; local localisation]

Suffering-driven empowerment combinations. Missions unlock abilities such as Material Fiction and Mastery of Entropy, as well as soul manipulation. The former gives a chance of extra development when developing a province; the latter requires extensive looting, casualties, ruler battles, and a Battle Mage Academy, then increases the gain from looting. Powerful abilities are not free buttons: they commit the country to more intense warfare over time. [Local script]

Ghost Fog and cultural assimilation. Mage towers can become nodes from which Ghost Fog spreads: your own side benefits from tax and order, while enemies become easier to conquer and suffer more unrest. Later decisions incorporate multiple Sarhali cultures into the Umbral system, but require the relevant culture, territory, and Shadow Pact conditions. This is coercive assimilation in service of imperial integration, not a pluralist route. [Local script]

Magical projects and planar convergence. The tree requires valuable magical resources, mage infrastructure, three unique projects, and a rift network advanced toward planar union. Some Shadow Empowerments are disabled during projects; the endgame then resolves the accumulated war, rifts, knowledge, and souls together. [Local script; official dev diary]

Campaign by phase

Opening: Kuende’s personal magic and shadow warriors give you initiative, but your territory is small and manpower is expensive. Continuous wars can quickly turn an advantage into an empty manpower pool. Stabilize the army, defeat nearby warlords, and spend religious resources on the omens and rituals that advance formation.

Formation: S30 forms through its event after completing its ten-mission prologue. Other countries using the general decision need the Shadow Pact faith, at least 30 qualifying non-swamp provinces in the specified Sarhal region, peace, free or tributary status, a government other than the Dakinshi Warlord government, and S70 to exist. For S30, delaying formation only postpones the much larger tree.

Umbral Empire: After formation, preserve the alliance with the Coven of Yezel Mora, unlock Shadow Empowerments, and turn conquered territory into essence capacity. Missions also demand high-development provinces, mage towers, production buildings, cultural assimilation, looting, and enormous casualty totals. If you pursue territory without preparing the magical and economic requirements, the middle and late game can repeatedly stall.

Endgame: Rifts and projects drive the campaign toward planar convergence. You must decide whether to accept the Coven’s intended ending or seek survival through betrayal. Neither outcome is a stable-governance epilogue; this is a magical expedition whose costs keep rising.

Formable and endgame

The S30 event invokes the shared formation effect: it changes the Tag to S90, raises the country to Empire rank, swaps non-generic missions, changes the government to a theocracy, and installs the dedicated magocracy reform and the Vile One. A general decision also allows other eligible Shadow Pact countries in Sarhal to form S90, but they do not have Kuende’s bespoke S30 prologue. This article therefore treats S30 → S90 as one continuous campaign chain while preserving the fact that S30 is not the only possible founder. [Local script]

The official dev diary introducing the formation concept in 2025 explicitly said S90 did not yet have a dedicated mission tree; a 2026 feature diary later presented Shadow Empowerments, the immortal ruler, magical projects, and large dynamic mission content. The current local files now contain the full dedicated tree. The older diary documents development history, not the present implementation. [Official dev diaries; local script]

Personality and recommendation

The v2.1 personality coordinates are Expansion 100/100 | Authoritarianism 95/100 | Magic ↔ Artifice 100/100 (100 = magic, 0 = artifice; theme intensity 100/100) | Pluralism 10/100.

The v2.1 values rating is Evil (0/100), with a worsening trajectory. The existing Chinese assessment cites kin-and-child sacrifice, deliberately manufactured suffering, looting, forced assimilation and planar sacrifice as institutional harms. The source-wording qualification above applies to the opening kin-and-child claim; this translation does not recalculate the assessment. Betraying the witches late does not erase what came before.

Recommended for players who enjoy extreme-villain narratives, very long trees, wide conquest, magical resource loadouts, dynamic objectives, and mage projects. Avoid if you dislike forced looting and sacrifice in the narrative, continuous war, high manpower costs, complex mission gates, or an ending that may resolve in failure itself.

Community experience

【Community view】An April 2026 guide to a development branch describes Umbral Covenant as a wide-expansion, religious, magical country. It warns that Shadow Empowerments are easy to overlook, cultural assimilation has many conditions, and shadow warriors rapidly consume manpower. This informs operational risks but does not supersede current local script values.

【Community view】A February 2026 development-version account describes a very powerful opening in which regional claims, looting, an immortal mage, and special troops can snowball; commenters note that manpower, corruption, reputation, and the Coven-related challenges make the costs catch up later. These accounts are compatible: the country is powerful, but power does not remove its mission and resource burdens.

Evidence limits

This article covers the local base Mod and localisation for v1.37.5.0, checked 2026-09-17. The S30 → S90 event chain, general formation conditions, 10 + 87 mission counts, empowerment upkeep, rifts, assimilation decisions, and two endings have current script evidence. Not every empowerment value, random ritual, or runtime ending event was audited.

The offline Wiki search did not return a dedicated article with substantive history for either Umbral Covenant or Death Bringing Cobra. Earlier research also cited Countries after the 1444 Divergence, which lists Umbral Covenant but does not supply a dedicated country history. The related Shadow Covenant entry (page_id=3304, revision_id=16330) concerns a separate secret organization. The related Coven of Yezel Mora entry (3945/27787) links Ilfanill’s cultivation of the Death Bringing Cobra leader and the child who became the Vile One, but does not establish that the Shadow Covenant and Umbral Covenant are identical. The two player accounts are explicitly from GitLab/development branches; current stable implementation follows the local scripts. See the evidence record for full provenance and remaining gaps.

National Ideas

The following reproduces the current local national-idea text and script effects. Traditions apply when the set is adopted; the seven ideas unlock in sequence as points are invested, and the ambition applies after all seven are unlocked. Only national ideas are listed: racial, government and mission bonuses are excluded. A successor idea set does not automatically stack with the earlier set. Idea descriptions may recall history or express future aspirations; they do not automatically establish events already completed in 1444. Names and complete descriptions use the current Mod’s English localisation. Alternative and predecessor/successor sets remain separately conditional, including whether new ideas are accepted on formation.

Effect display units inherited from the source data are reproduced for parity, not revalidated here. Suspicious percentages and script-valued effects require separate review; raw values are shown below.

Death Bringing Cobra (S30) — Death Bringing Cobra Ideas

Set ID: S30_ideas. Source: project-verified Mod script (public artifact omits local path and line offsets).

Applicability condition (source script):

    trigger = {
        tag = S30 #Death Bringing Cobra
    }

Death Bringing Cobra Traditions

  • Infantry combat ability: +10% (infantry_power; raw value 0.10).

  • National tax modifier: +15% (global_tax_modifier; raw value 0.15).

1. Heirs of Bwa Dakinshi

Many centuries ago, Bamaliwuni was a place scattered with many squabbling tribes, very unlike the warlords that developed later. They lived under the yoke of the Djinnakah Sultanate that established tribute over each of them, controlling the entire region from their outposts at the mouths of large rivers. When this empire collapsed, a power vacuum emerged, throwing the tribes into endless war that ended in a formation of a state that people call Bwa Dakinshi, the same one that the warlords struggle endlessly to recreate. But the part of that history that the warlords do not remember is that this state still lives.

The clan and the heirs of the great unifier Mauya Venomrisker are still standing, hidden in the mountains, despite the many rebellions that faced them; as long as they stand, no one can dare name themselves Bwa Dakinshi.

  • Legitimacy: +1 (legitimacy; raw value 1).

  • Devotion: +1 (devotion; raw value 1).

  • Horde unity: +1 (horde_unity; raw value 1).

  • Republican tradition: +0.3 (republican_tradition; raw value 0.3).

2. The Tainted Lineage

Not so long ago, the clan of Death Bringing Cobra was on the verge of regaining their lost heritage. The entire north of Bamaliwuni stood open to them after their capture of Inshibonde and no one could stand against them; the sprawling state of Katidariga had just collapsed, the warlords of Gumti had already succumbed and offered their services, while Kaziradoka stayed encircled with no allies to support them.

But no one suspected the enemy to come from within. The traitor named Kwizera struck in a swift coup that murdered most of our clan. The remnants escaped to the high mountains, led by Kuende, the first wife of the matriarch. Yet in her guidance, a dark truth was hidden, as she sold herself to the Hags a long time ago. No one is truly aware of the scale of the danger she truly poses, but one thing is known. The child she took with herself, the true heir to the Bwa Dakinshi, bears the same dark aura as her, and only time will tell what dark thoughts possess Her mind.

  • War exhaustion: -0.03 (war_exhaustion; raw value -0.03).

3. The Poor and The Strong

The reality of a warlord society is ruthless. Competitors are plenty and the resources scarce and centered in few places. Those who are not strong enough find themselves working for the sole benefit of their local warlords, while those who dare try to fight the existing hierarchy, duel their way into the higher position amongst the Munitaragomo to hopefully reach the top of the hierarchy as the Vitaragomo of the warband. While this means that only competent fighters advance to the top, this also adds to the instability of the region, as warlords incessantly rebel against their former overlords.

  • General cost: -15% (general_cost; raw value -0.15).

4. Unfiltered Mockery

It isn’t really a secret that warlords largely despise each other. The net of personal grudges between the Vitaragomo has been dense for years with few ends unconnected, effectively stymying any attempt at diplomacy that is not a simple demand for capitulation. So far goes this devotion to not liking each other that some animosities are now built artificially, by a peculiar custom that emerged something over hundred years ago.

The lesser warlords sit down with the Vitaragomo near a large table. Some of them see paper for the first time in their lives, as they hear the name of the warlord that is the topic of the meeting. For the following six hours, the meeting will proceed as its members write out a series of convoluted and obscene insults towards a certain warlord; this is then sent to the victim, who upon delivery must read it aloud to the laughter of his subjects, risking great shame if he doesn’t.

  • Power projection from insults: +1 (power_projection_from_insults; raw value 1).

5. Freshly Made Beans and Weapons

The demand for iron for weapons and luxuries for the rich never runs out. Despite the poor state of the economy and the dangers that the region’s trade routes bear, there are still traders brave and insane enough to traverse the lands of Bamaliwuni, looking to secure its riches and carry them to the port cities. The upside is worth it though, as those who manage to make the trip find themselves richer than most Dakinshi, able to afford a lavish lifestyle for the rest of their lives just with a few ventures.

  • Trade range: +50% (trade_range_modifier; raw value 0.5).

  • Yearly inflation reduction: +0.1% (inflation_reduction; raw value 0.1).

6. War Druids

Previously serving as the spiritual leaders of the Dakinshi society, the druids of the Beast Memory serve as the reminders of once broken link between humans and animals. Brought up from those magically gifted across the land, they organize themselves at the natural meeting points of animal herds, protecting these vital positions against any interference that would disrupt the natural order.

While typically peaceful in their behavior, the times of strife have proven dangerous enough to change some of the druids' stance to a more offensive one, joining the many warlords of the land in a proactive effort to keep out everyone who does not care about the environment.

  • Shock damage: +5% (shock_damage; raw value 0.05).

  • English translation: [Country.GetMageName]: +5% (mages_loyalty_modifier; raw value 0.05).

7. Dreams of a Reborn Empire

Across the land, there is a common impetus driving every warlord’s mind. A desire to win, to squash one’s opponents under their feet, best them in battle, lay upon their corpses and dance on their graves. The dream of an empire that toppled not so long ago as to be forgotten, but long enough to be romanticised through second-hand nostalgia. The ambition to become something bigger, to be remembered, to be unlike the others. To make oneself known, feared, respected and acknowledged as the single, true unifier to the empire they forged with blood, sweat and tears. This will be the ultimate price of the new Bwa Dakinshi.

  • Prestige: +1 (prestige; raw value 1).

Death Bringing Cobra Ambition

  • Leader siege: +1 (leader_siege; raw value 1).

Umbral Covenant (S90) — Umbral Covenant Ideas

Set ID: S90_ideas. Source: project-verified Mod script (public artifact omits local path and line offsets).

Applicability condition (source script):

    trigger = {
        tag = S90
        NOT = { has_country_flag = S30_warlordism_over }
    }

Umbral Covenant Traditions

  • Morale damage: +15% (morale_damage; raw value 0.15).

  • Religious power modifier: +10% (church_power_modifier; raw value 0.1).

1. The Vile One

She was taken as a child by the Night Hag’s Coven. She was not the only one. If one of the Coven detected a baby had been born with incredible latent powers, they would do whatever it took to steal her away and raise her themselves: strike a deal with the parents in exchange for food or power, lure the child away when she was alone, every ace in their collective sleeves shamelessly played. It is estimated that hundreds were whisked away by the Night Hags over the centuries they have plagued Halann, children of every nation and every race.

Such a child was then raised by the hags to be used as a pawn in their nefarious plans for Sarhal. If the child failed to reach expectations, or developed a sudden conscience, they were discarded. The hags’ ideal pawn may have taken hundreds of years to mold, but once complete, would be a weapon they could send forth to carry out their dark bidding independently. The Vile One, as this child would be dubbed, would have the power to unite all peoples beneath her inescapable will.

Human, lizardfolk, gnoll: all would be drawn to her power and unite under her.

  • Number of accepted cultures: +3 (num_accepted_cultures; raw value 3).

  • Promote culture cost: -25% (promote_culture_cost; raw value -0.25).

2. Shadows Deliver

Shadow Pact is not an inherently evil faith. There is solace to be found in the acceptance of death and the powerlessness you have over your fate. Those who speak of Shadow Pact’s virtue expound upon the peace and clarity you feel in life when you know those of the shadow plane will look after you in death. Yet there is a second face to Shadow Pact. One in which its followers seek not just solace in death, but power over life. Accepting the power of those of the shadow plane, these practitioners call such power into our own.

The Vile One is perhaps the greatest symbol of this face of Shadow Pact. One who was created by the most powerful creatures of the Shadow Plane. Her sole purpose is to grant a nation the power to seize control over all that they wish to call theirs.

  • True faith tolerance: +2 (tolerance_own; raw value 2).

3. The Fog

A nation ruled over by The Vile One changes. A fog spreads like a suffocating blanket over its lands. This fog spreads slowly, blotting out the sun for weeks on end, and obscuring vision such that even leaving your home can be dangerous. Neighbouring countries are not safe from its impact, as the fog neither knows nor cares for borders.

The Vile One’s armies marched under the protection of this fog. This became such a well-known strategy of their armies that people began to panic and flee if the fog spread into their towns, for they knew that meant her armies would soon follow.

  • Fabricate-claim cost: -25% (fabricate_claims_cost; raw value -0.25).

4. Sarhal Was Not Ready

While Sarhal had seen many great conquerors, The Vile One was different. There was no attempt to seek allies, no diplomatic formalities, not even any recognition that other towns or nations had existing hierarchies or rulers through which negotiations could be channelled. Her armies simply marched across borders, struck down any who resisted, and established control over their newly conquered lands. Any dissent was crushed and all previous order was upended. Only those who pledged their allegiance to The Vile One were placed in any position of power. There was no shortage of those who would, even in those areas newly conquered. For they knew, ever since the fog arrived, that this day was coming. There was no stopping the spread of shadow.

  • Core-creation cost: -10% (core_creation; raw value -0.1).

5. Groupthink

In the core homelands where The Vile One first made herself known, operations were curiously calm and orderly. If you received the call to join the army, it was an honor. If you were placed in administrative positions, that was your duty. If you were a simple laborer or farmer, that too was your role and it was as important as any. Acceptance was absolute. Those who did not agree, or attempted to undermine the cause in any way, disappeared into the fog. Everyone thought everyone else supported the cause, so they did too.

  • Yearly corruption: -0.1 (yearly_corruption; raw value -0.1).

  • Manpower from true faith provinces: +10% (manpower_in_true_faith_provinces; raw value 0.1).

6. When the Riots Started

When The Vile One fell and the fog was lifted, enemy soldiers attempted to find ringleaders of operations. They captured mayors and chieftains of towns, spoke to villagers and soldiers, and tried to interrogate everyone in the nation to ask why they had sided with a being so obviously evil and destructive. They brought accounts of the horrors her armies had committed, and evidence of what the true final goal of the Night Hags was.

Yet their words did not seem to have any effect. The locals were far too preoccupied with the horrific state of their lands, the decay that they had seemingly only just noticed. The rot was not merely a result of invasion, either. Barren fields, crumbling housing, and decrepit local facilities had just become an accepted norm. Only after her death did the riots start.

  • Missionary strength: +2% (global_missionary_strength; raw value 0.02).

  • Stability cost modifier: -10% (stability_cost_modifier; raw value -0.1).

7. Her True Goal

Scholars of Sarhaly history have often debated over the true goals of The Vile One. A growing body of evidence suggests that the simple explanation - that she was simply doing the bidding of the Night Hags - was not a satisfactory answer. It was the actions of The Vile One that caused all of Sarhal to erupt into war, not the infamous ritual the Night Hags had started, for that ritual only started several years after the war began. Military historians have also noted the complete lack of coordination between Yezel Mora and The Vile One. Yes, they fought the same enemies, but not once did they ever fight together. Nobody ever asked her what she was trying to achieve. It would not have crossed anyone’s minds to do so.

  • Maximum Absolutism: +10 (max_absolutism; raw value 10).

Umbral Covenant Ambition

  • Governing Capacity Modifier: +20% (governing_capacity_modifier; raw value 0.2).

3. Snake In The Fog

It was the eminent Adzalani researcher Tzaaska Cursebreaker who first compellingly identified Kuende as a possible mother for the Vile One. Beyond the broadly correct ethnicity and the emergence of her realm from Dakinshi, Kuende was a known mage who emerged as leader of the moribund Death Bringing Cobra clan before the eventual co-opting of said clan by the Vile One’s Umbral Covenant.

While historians were initially wont to view this shift from clan to Covenant as a subversion or coup, Tzasska argued that Kuende had deliberately prepared her realm for her estranged daughter. As Vitaragomo, Kuende seems to have hoarded raid-wealth, ritual resources and materiél for a purpose she would not explain, directly against the wishes of her own advisors and clanmates. Kuende’s reign of terror was significant in her own right, and the scorched earth tactics pursued by the Vile One, while different in the particulars, seem to echo Kuende’s own.

  • Raze power gain: +0.2 (raze_power_gain; raw value 0.2).

7. Omnicidal Venom

We know nothing of the Vile One’s intentions; her apparently vast memory and her penchant for telepathic matrices with her closest followers means that her coterie wrote very little down, and in the final days her most devoted adherents made great effort to destroy as many of her records as possible. Kuende, on the other hand, leaves a limited but compelling record. Traumatised by the near-annihilation and humiliation of her clan, Kuende appears to have turned against the very concept of honour itself.

Did the daughter know something of the mother’s will, her utter and complete nihilism? There is no evidence that Kuende ever presented a baby at court, though she alluded obliquely at times to an heir, and was unconcerned with matters of succession. Tzasska Cursebreaker argued in her ‘Addenda’ that the two women likely never met: whatever hatred Kuende felt for Halann, she entrusted to the hags to inculcate in her daughter.

  • Maximum absolutism: +15% (max_absolutism_effect; raw value 0.15).
